trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Vatican City, Borgo district Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use the morning to rest on the plane and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Leonardo Express train or the cheaper FL1 regional train to Roma Termini, then connect via Metro Line A to Ottaviano station (closest to Vatican/Borgo district). Check in to your boutique stay in the Borgo district. Once settled, take a leisurely stroll along Via della Conciliazione toward St. Peter's Square — admire the iconic colonnade and the exterior of St. Peter's Basilica for free. Explore the charming Borgo Pio pedestrian alley lined with cafes and souvenir shops.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Borgo neighborhood to get your bearings. Head to the nearby Castel Sant'Angelo for a scenic walk along the Tiber River at sunset — the exterior and bridge (Ponte Sant'Angelo) are free to enjoy. Grab a gelato from a local gelateria on Via della Conciliazione.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable panino or supplì (fried rice ball) from a local alimentari or bar near the Borgo district — budget around €5–8.
meals.dinner: Trattatoria Pizzarium-style slice pizza or a sit-down meal at a budget trattoria in Borgo Pio. Try 'Il Sorpasso' or a local pizzeria al taglio for a filling meal under €12–15.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Purchase a 48-hour or 72-hour Roma Pass or a metro/bus multi-day ticket at Termini to save on transport costs throughout the trip. Validate your ticket every time you board public transport.

day_by_day.morning: Start early (book in advance — free entry to St. Peter's Basilica is always free). Visit St. Peter's Basilica first thing in the morning to beat the crowds. Climb to the top of the dome (€8 with stairs, €10 with elevator) for a breathtaking panoramic view of Rome. Explore the stunning interior including Michelangelo's Pietà at no extra cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel (book online in advance to avoid queues — entry ~€17 with online booking). Marvel at Raphael's Rooms and the awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling painted by Michelangelo. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the vast museum corridors filled with ancient sculptures and Renaissance masterpieces.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Borgo district and relax. Head to the lively Prati neighborhood (a 10-minute walk) for an aperitivo hour — many bars offer free snacks with a drink (spritz ~€5–7). Explore the local streets and window-shop along Via Cola di Rienzo.

meals.breakfast: Grab a classic Italian breakfast at a local bar near your hotel — espresso and cornetto (croissant) for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Vatican Museums cafeteria (budget option) or pack a sandwich from a nearby alimentari to save money — aim for under €8.
meals.dinner: Head to Prati neighborhood for a budget-friendly dinner. Try 'Osteria dell'Angelo' for classic Roman pasta dishes like cacio e pepe or amatriciana — expect to spend €15–20 including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays (except last Sunday of the month when entry is free but extremely crowded). Tuesday is a great day to visit. Book Vatican Museums tickets online at least a few days in advance to skip the long queues and save time.

day_by_day.morning: Take Metro Line A from Ottaviano to Spagna station. Visit the Spanish Steps (free) in the morning before it gets too crowded. Explore the elegant Piazza di Spagna and the surrounding streets. Walk to the nearby Trevi Fountain (about 10 minutes on foot) — toss a coin for good luck. Admire the baroque masterpiece and take photos before the tourist crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Pantheon (about 15 minutes on foot) — entry is now €5 but absolutely worth it for this remarkably preserved 2,000-year-old Roman temple. Spend time in the surrounding Piazza della Rotonda. Afterward, explore the bohemian Campo de' Fiori market square (market runs until ~2pm) and the adjacent Piazza Navona (free) with its stunning Bernini fountains.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the historic Jewish Ghetto neighborhood and cross the Tiber to Trastevere — Rome's most atmospheric neighborhood. Explore the cobblestone streets, admire the Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free), and soak up the lively evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Bar near hotel — espresso and pastry for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab street food near Campo de' Fiori — supplì, pizza al taglio, or a porchetta sandwich for €5–8. The market vendors often have affordable fresh produce too.
meals.dinner: Dine in Trastevere at a budget trattoria. Look for fixed-price 'menù turistico' options or try 'Da Enzo al 29' for authentic Roman cuisine — budget €15–20 per person including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — today involves significant walking across Rome's historic center. Carry a reusable water bottle and refill it at Rome's free drinking fountains ('nasoni') scattered throughout the city. Trastevere is very lively in the evenings — great for people-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Take Metro Line B from Termini (transfer at Repubblica from Line A) to Colosseo station. Visit the Colosseum (book online in advance — ~€16 including Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, valid for 2 days). Explore this iconic ancient amphitheater and learn about its gladiatorial history. The combined ticket also covers the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Roman Forum — the ancient heart of the Roman Empire — and climb Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Forum and Circus Maximus. These are all included in your combined ticket. Afterward, walk to the Circus Maximus (free exterior) and then to the Aventine Hill to visit the Knights of Malta keyhole (free) — peek through for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take a bus back toward the city center. Visit the atmospheric Testaccio neighborhood, known as Rome's foodie district. Browse the Testaccio Market (closes by 3pm) if you arrive early enough, or explore the neighborhood's trattorias and wine bars in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Bar near hotel — espresso and cornetto for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a nearby alimentari or grab street food near the Colosseum — avoid the overpriced tourist restaurants immediately adjacent to the site. Budget €6–10.
meals.dinner: Eat in Testaccio — try 'Flavio al Velavevodetto' for traditional Roman offal dishes (or classic pasta if adventurous eating isn't your thing) at reasonable prices, or grab a meal at the Testaccio Market food stalls for €10–15.

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum area gets extremely hot in summer — bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. The combined Colosseum/Forum/Palatine ticket is the best value in Rome. Consider visiting the free Circus Maximus and Aventine keyhole as bonus stops that most tourists skip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery (MUST book in advance — entry €15, timed entry slots of 2 hours, strictly enforced). This is one of Rome's greatest art treasures, housing Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings in a stunning villa. Take Metro Line A to Spagna and walk up through Villa Borghese park (free) to reach the gallery. The park itself is a lovely green escape.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, explore the vast Villa Borghese park on foot or rent a rowboat on the small lake (budget activity, ~€5–8). Walk or take a bus to Piazza del Popolo (free) — admire the twin baroque churches and the Egyptian obelisk. Climb the Pincian Hill terrace for a free panoramic view of Rome's skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Flaminio or Prati area for the evening. Visit the free exterior of the Ara Pacis museum and stroll along the Tiber riverbanks. Enjoy Rome's Friday evening passeggiata (evening stroll) culture with locals.

meals.breakfast: Bar near hotel — espresso and pastry for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese park — pick up supplies from a local alimentari or market beforehand. Fresh bread, cheese, prosciutto, and fruit for under €10.
meals.dinner: Return to Prati neighborhood for dinner. Try a local pizzeria for a classic Roman thin-crust pizza — 'Pizzarium Bonci' (Gabriele Bonci's famous pizza al taglio) on Via della Meloria is a must-try for pizza lovers, with slices from €3–5 each.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance — book as soon as possible, ideally before your trip. The gallery only allows 360 visitors at a time in 2-hour slots. The picnic in Villa Borghese is one of Rome's great budget pleasures — locals do it all the time.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-visited but fascinating neighborhood of Pigneto or take a bus to the Appian Way (Via Appia Antica) — one of Rome's oldest roads, lined with ancient tombs and catacombs. Visit the Catacombs of San Callisto or San Sebastiano (~€8 each, guided tours only) for an eerie and fascinating underground experience. Rent a bike along the Appian Way for a scenic and affordable ride (~€5–10/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center and visit the Capitoline Museums (€15) — the world's oldest public museums, housing incredible ancient Roman sculptures including the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue and the Capitoline Wolf. The rooftop terrace offers a stunning free view over the Roman Forum. Alternatively, if budget is tight, visit the free Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano (Rome's oldest basilica) and the nearby Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your second-to-last evening revisiting your favorite spots. Head to Campo de' Fiori or Piazza Navona for the lively Saturday evening atmosphere. Enjoy a final gelato crawl — compare flavors from different gelaterias (look for 'artigianale' signs for authentic artisan gelato, ~€2.50–4 per cone).

meals.breakfast: Bar near hotel — espresso and cornetto for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget lunch near the Appian Way or city center — a simple pasta dish at a local trattoria away from tourist hotspots for €8–12.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for a Saturday treat — find a local trattoria in the Trastevere or Pigneto neighborhoods for a proper sit-down Roman meal with antipasto, pasta, and house wine for €20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a busy day in Rome — popular sites will be crowded. The Appian Way is best visited by bike or on foot and is quieter than central Rome. The Capitoline Museums are often overlooked by tourists in favor of the Vatican but are equally impressive and historically significant.

day_by_day.morning: On the last Sunday of the month, Vatican Museums offer free entry (very crowded — arrive extremely early). If this is not the last Sunday, visit the beautiful and free Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere for Sunday morning mass — a deeply atmospheric Roman experience. Alternatively, explore the Sunday morning Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (one of Europe's largest flea markets, open until 2pm) for vintage finds and local color.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Borgo district and take a final walk through your home neighborhood. Visit the free Castel Sant'Angelo interior if you haven't already (€14 entry) for Roman, medieval, and Renaissance history and rooftop views of Rome. Pack your bags and do any last-minute souvenir shopping along Borgo Pio or Via della Conciliazione — look for affordable local ceramics, prints, or food products.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner in the Prati neighborhood. Reflect on your Roman adventure over a classic meal — try suppli, cacio e pepe pasta, and tiramisu for dessert. Head back to the hotel to prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Italian breakfast at your favorite local bar — espresso and cornetto for €2–3. Savor the ritual!
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Porta Portese market area or a quick pizza al taglio — budget €6–8.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Prati — a classic Roman trattoria meal with pasta, secondi, and house wine. Budget €18–22 per person for a memorable send-off.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure flight time and plan your airport transfer accordingly. The FL1 regional train from Roma Trastevere or Roma Tiburtina to Fiumicino is cheaper than the Leonardo Express (€8 vs €14) but takes slightly longer. Leave extra time for Sunday transport which may run on reduced schedules. Keep some cash for tips (not obligatory in Italy but appreciated — rounding up the bill is common).

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini, then connect by taxi or bus to your boutique stay in the Borgo district near Vatican City. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in your neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Neighborhood Orientation Walk — After settling in, take a leisurely self-guided stroll through the Borgo district. Walk along Via della Conciliazione toward St. Peter's Square for your first iconic view of the basilica's facade. Admire the colonnade and the square without the full tourist rush of a planned tour. Pop into a local tabacchi or alimentari to grab a map and any essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Casual Dinner in Prati — Head to the lively Prati neighborhood (a 10-minute walk from Borgo), a local favorite with excellent mid-range trattorias. Enjoy a relaxed first Roman dinner to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and cornetto at the airport or on arrival — no formal breakfast scheduled today.
meals.lunch: Light bite near the hotel upon arrival — try a panino or pizza al taglio from a local bakery in Borgo (€5–10).
meals.dinner: Trattoria Pizzarium area or Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — try classic Roman pasta dishes like cacio e pepe or carbonara, with house wine (€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Do not book any timed entry tickets for today. Confirm all advance bookings for the rest of the week. June in Rome can be warm (25–32°C), so carry water and wear light layers.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (Pre-Booked Experience) — Begin your art immersion with an early-morning timed entry to the Vatican Museums, ideally booked for 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Marvel at the Gallery of Maps, the Raphael Rooms, and culminate in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. This is a 3–4 hour experience; comfortable shoes are essential.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Dome Climb — Exit the Museums and walk directly into St. Peter's Basilica (free entry). Spend time with Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's magnificent baldachin. Optionally climb the dome (€8 with elevator, €6 on foot) for sweeping panoramic views over Rome. Rest briefly at a café in Piazza Risorgimento afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk (Guided Experience) — Cross the Tiber for this curated food walk through Trastevere's cobblestone streets. Sample supplì, artichokes alla romana, local cheeses, and pair with regional wines. A perfect sensory introduction to Roman culinary culture.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a nearby Prati café — cappuccino and cornetto, the quintessential Roman start (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near St. Peter's Square — try Pizzarium Bonci on Via della Meloria for Rome's finest pizza al taglio (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience — multiple tastings across several stops (experience cost typically €60–80 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially in June. Dress code enforced: no bare shoulders or shorts above the knee for the Basilica. The Trastevere walk typically starts around 18:30–19:00; confirm timing with the operator.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour (Pre-Booked Experience) — Take a taxi or bus to Villa Borghese for a timed-entry guided tour of this intimate jewel-box museum. Admire Bernini's breathtaking sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases. Entry is strictly limited to 2-hour slots; book well ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Piazza del Popolo — After the gallery, enjoy a relaxed walk through the beautiful Villa Borghese park. Rent a rowboat on the lake (€5–8) or simply stroll. Descend to Piazza del Popolo to see the twin baroque churches and the Egyptian obelisk. Walk or take a taxi to the Spanish Steps area for a brief visit.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Pigneto or Testaccio district — venture to Testaccio, Rome's traditional working-class food neighborhood, for an authentic Roman dinner featuring offal-based classics or simpler grilled meats if preferred.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel in Borgo/Prati — try Bar San Pietro or similar for a classic Roman breakfast (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up supplies from a nearby deli or Prati market: cheeses, cured meats, bread, fruit (€12–18 total).
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto or Roscioli Salumeria in Testaccio — Roman classics in a relaxed trattoria setting (€30–40 per person with wine).

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery is one of Rome's most strictly ticketed venues — reservations are mandatory and must be made weeks in advance. Arrive 15 minutes early. The gallery allows a maximum of 360 visitors per 2-hour session.

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class (Full Experience) — Head to the vibrant Campo de' Fiori morning market to select fresh seasonal produce with your chef instructor. Learn to identify local Roman ingredients — artichokes, guanciale, pecorino, fresh pasta. Then transfer to a nearby kitchen for a hands-on cooking class preparing a 3-course Roman meal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jewish Ghetto & Largo di Torre Argentina — After your cooking class lunch, walk to the nearby Jewish Ghetto, one of Rome's most historically layered neighborhoods. Visit the Portico d'Ottavia ruins and browse artisan shops. Stop at Largo di Torre Argentina — the ancient temple ruins where Julius Caesar was assassinated — now a cat sanctuary.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Stroll & Gelato on the Pantheon & Navona Circuit — Walk to the Pantheon (free exterior viewing in the evening; entry fee applies if open), then continue to the stunning Piazza Navona with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers. End the evening with artisan gelato from a trusted gelateria.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before heading to Campo de' Fiori (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class — you eat what you cook! (Typically part of the experience fee, €70–100 per person).
meals.dinner: Gelateria di Campo near Campo de' Fiori for gelato (€3–5), or a light aperitivo spread at a wine bar near Piazza Navona (€15–20).

day_by_day.notes: The Campo de' Fiori market runs Monday–Saturday, mornings only (typically 8:00–14:00). Book the cooking class in advance. This is a more relaxed afternoon and evening — intentionally lighter to balance the intensive morning activity.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Visit — Take the metro or a short taxi to the Colosseum area. Enter via the combined ticket (Colosseum, Roman Forum, Palatine Hill — €18–22). Start at the Roman Forum to walk through the ancient civic heart of Rome — the Sacred Way, the Temple of Saturn, the Arch of Titus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palatine Hill Sunset Visit (Extended Afternoon) — Climb Palatine Hill, birthplace of Rome and home of the imperial palaces. Explore the Farnese Gardens and enjoy panoramic views over the Forum below and the Circus Maximus. This is best experienced in the late afternoon when the light is golden and crowds thin. The Colosseum exterior can be admired from outside if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo & Dinner in Testaccio or Aventine Hill — Wind down in the Testaccio neighborhood with a classic Roman aperitivo. Then enjoy a relaxed dinner at a neighborhood osteria.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Trattoria near the Colosseum — avoid tourist traps; try Ristorante Aroma or a simple local spot on Via Capo d'Africa (€20–30 per person).
meals.dinner: Da Remo in Testaccio for Rome's best thin-crust pizza in a bustling, authentic setting (€15–20 per person) or Osteria Fernanda for a more refined experience (€35–45 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum timed entry separately if you wish to go inside — it requires an additional reservation and often sells out. The Roman Forum and Palatine Hill combined ticket is excellent value. June evenings are long (sunset around 20:30–21:00), making the Palatine Hill afternoon experience particularly magical.

day_by_day.morning: Capitoline Museums & Piazza del Campidoglio — Visit the world's oldest public museums, designed by Michelangelo. See the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and stunning ancient Roman sculpture collections. The terrace offers one of Rome's best views over the Roman Forum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trastevere Afternoon Exploration — Cross the Tiber and spend a relaxed afternoon exploring Trastevere's charming streets in daylight. Visit the Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free, stunning golden mosaics), browse artisan boutiques, and sit in a piazza with a cold Aperol Spritz.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Splurge Dinner — Treat yourself to a slightly elevated dinner at one of Rome's celebrated mid-range restaurants, celebrating your week in the Eternal City.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Prati — try a sfogliatella or maritozzo con la panna for something special (€5–7).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Trastevere — Da Enzo al 29 for Roman classics like cacio e pepe and carciofi alla romana in a beloved local trattoria (€25–35 per person).
meals.dinner: Ristorante Glass Hostaria (Trastevere) for creative modern Roman cuisine, or Il Sorpasso in Prati for a stylish wine bar dinner with charcuterie and seasonal dishes (€40–55 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday mornings at Campo de' Fiori market are particularly lively if you want to revisit. Trastevere on Saturday evenings becomes very busy with locals and tourists alike — embrace the energy. Book the splurge dinner in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Quiet Sunday Morning — Rome on Sunday mornings is magical and peaceful. Walk to St. Peter's Square for the Papal Angelus blessing at noon (free, from the Pope's window — check Vatican schedule). Alternatively, visit one of Rome's lesser-known baroque churches such as Sant'Ignazio di Loyola or Santa Maria della Vittoria (Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last Wanders & Shopping — Spend your final afternoon revisiting a favorite neighborhood or piazza. Browse Via del Corso or the artisan shops near Campo de' Fiori for souvenirs. Pick up quality Italian food gifts: pasta, olive oil, cured meats from a deli. Enjoy a final gelato at Giolitti or Fatamorgana.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed Farewell Dinner & Packing — Enjoy a simple, heartfelt last dinner near the hotel in Prati or Borgo before packing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Special Sunday breakfast — try Pasticceria Siciliana Svizzera in Prati for pastries, or a hotel breakfast if included (€6–10).
meals.lunch: Light Sunday lunch at a local trattoria in Prati — many Romans do a long Sunday lunch; join the tradition with pasta and a carafe of house wine (€20–30 per person).
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a trusted neighborhood spot near the hotel — keep it simple and sentimental. Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati is a beloved local classic (€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Many museums are closed or have reduced hours on Sundays — check in advance. The Papal Angelus is typically at 12:00 noon from the Vatican; verify the schedule on the Vatican website as it varies. Allow extra time on departure day for airport transfer — the Leonardo Express to Fiumicino takes about 32 minutes from Roma Termini.

meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel or a quick stop at a premium Borgo café such as Caffè San Pietro for a panino and Aperol Spritz upon settling in.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Ristorante Il Matriciano (Via dei Gracchi) — a historic Roman institution beloved for cacio e pepe, amatriciana, and seasonal Roman specialties in an intimate setting.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Confirm all upcoming experience bookings with your hotel concierge. Request a Vatican Museums skip-the-line confirmation and arrange a private guide for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel Private Tour (09:00–12:30): Begin with an exclusive early-access or small-group premium guided tour of one of the world's greatest art collections. Move through the Gallery of Maps, the Raphael Rooms, and culminate in a breathtaking private moment in the Sistine Chapel admiring Michelangelo's ceiling. Your expert art historian guide will bring centuries of history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit St. Peter's Basilica (included in the Vatican complex) and climb the dome for sweeping panoramic views over Rome. Afterward, explore Castel Sant'Angelo — a short walk along the Tiber — and its museum tracing its history from imperial mausoleum to papal fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk (19:00–22:00): Cross the Tiber into the enchanting Trastevere neighborhood for a guided gourmet walk sampling supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes alla giudia, aged pecorino, and local wines in some of the district's most celebrated spots.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast or visit Dal Bolognese–style café near Borgo for cornetto, cappuccino, and fresh-squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Vatican Museums café or a refined quick bite at Pizzarium Bonci (Via della Meloria) — Rome's most acclaimed gourmet pizza al taglio.
meals.dinner: Conclude the Trastevere food walk with a seated dinner at Tonnarello or Da Enzo al 29 — intimate, rustic-chic trattorias serving elevated Roman classics with excellent house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the Vatican and Trastevere walk. The Sistine Chapel prohibits photography — be prepared to simply absorb the experience. Book the Trastevere evening walk through a premium culinary tour operator for a private or semi-private group.

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class (09:00–13:30): Begin at the vibrant Campo de' Fiori morning market, selecting the finest seasonal produce, fresh herbs, local cheeses, and cured meats with your private chef guide. Transfer to a premium cooking studio (or a curated private kitchen) for a hands-on class preparing Roman dishes such as cacio e pepe, supplì, and a seasonal vegetable contorno — concluding with a sit-down lunch featuring everything you've created.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-lunch, walk through the Jewish Ghetto — Rome's oldest neighborhood — and visit the stunning Portico d'Ottavia ruins. Continue to the Pantheon for a profound encounter with ancient Roman engineering. Explore the Piazza della Rotonda and surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury aperitivo hour at the rooftop bar of Hotel de la Minerve or Hotel Raphael for elevated Negronis and panoramic views, followed by dinner in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Forno Campo de' Fiori bakery — Rome's most iconic bakery, open from early morning with exceptional pizza bianca and pastries.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the cooking class — a full sit-down meal of dishes prepared during the class, paired with local wines.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Convivio Troiani (Piazza dei Massimi) — one of Rome's most celebrated Michelin-starred restaurants offering creative fine dining rooted in Italian culinary tradition, with an exceptional wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class should be pre-booked with a reputable culinary school such as Città del Gusto or a private chef service. Campo de' Fiori market runs until approximately 14:00 — arrive early for the best selection.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Private Art Tour (09:00–11:00): Secure a coveted timed-entry reservation (mandatory) for an intimate guided experience of Bernini's breathtaking baroque sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — alongside Caravaggio's dramatic canvases and works by Raphael and Titian. With a private art historian, explore the nuanced stories behind each masterpiece in this jewel-box villa museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the magnificent Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's most elegant park — for a picturesque afternoon. Visit the nearby Piazza del Popolo with its twin baroque churches, then walk the fashionable Via Condotti for luxury shopping (Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi flagship stores). Climb the Spanish Steps for a classic Roman panorama.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo at the legendary Caffè Greco (Via Condotti) — Rome's oldest café, frequented by Keats, Byron, and Goethe — followed by a refined dinner in the Prati neighborhood near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a visit to a premium Prati-area café such as Pasticceria De Bellis for exquisite pastries and espresso.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at the Borghese Gallery café terrace or nearby Ristorante Baby (Hotel Aldrovandi) — a sophisticated restaurant overlooking private gardens, perfect for a leisurely midday meal.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Osteria dell'Angelo or the acclaimed Settimio all'Arancio — intimate Roman osterie serving elevated traditional Roman cuisine in a warm, candlelit atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery strictly limits visitors to 2-hour slots and sells out weeks in advance — confirm your reservation before the trip. The gallery is a short taxi or tram ride from Borgo. Bring a light layer for the air-conditioned gallery interior.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Morning Visit (09:00–12:00): Beat the midday heat with an early private guided tour of the ancient heart of the Roman Empire. Walk the Via Sacra through the Roman Forum, exploring the Temple of Saturn, the Arch of Titus, and the House of the Vestal Virgins. Ascend Palatine Hill — birthplace of Rome — for sweeping views over the Forum and Circus Maximus. Your guide will animate the grandeur of Imperial Rome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum with a premium access ticket (arena floor or underground access available with advance booking) for an unparalleled perspective on Rome's most iconic monument. Afterward, explore the Celio neighborhood's hidden gems — the Basilica of San Clemente with its extraordinary layers of history descending to a 1st-century Roman house.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the Aventine Hill at the Knights of Malta Keyhole — a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome — followed by dinner in Testaccio, Rome's authentic culinary neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or stop at a local Borgo bar for espresso and a fresh cornetto before heading to the Forum.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Aroma (Palazzo Manfredi) — Rome's most dramatic dining experience with a private terrace offering unobstructed Colosseum views. A true luxury splurge for an unforgettable setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) — a beloved, critically acclaimed Roman trattoria built into the ancient Monte Testaccio, serving exceptional offal dishes, cacio e pepe, and seasonal Roman classics.

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum underground or arena floor access well in advance — these premium tickets sell out quickly. Ristorante Aroma requires reservations weeks ahead. Wear sunscreen and a hat for the Forum and Palatine Hill — limited shade in June.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or deeper neighborhood immersion: Spend a leisurely morning exploring the Prati neighborhood — Rome's elegant, grid-planned district adjacent to your hotel. Visit the Mercato Trionfale (Via Andrea Doria) — Rome's largest covered food market — for a sensory feast of local produce, truffles, aged cheeses, and cured meats. Browse the market with a local food guide for premium tastings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private art studio or gallery visit in the Trastevere or Prati area — arrange through your concierge a behind-the-scenes visit to a contemporary Roman artist's studio or a private collection. Alternatively, visit the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj for its extraordinary private art collection (Velázquez, Caravaggio, Raphael) rarely crowded even on weekends.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private wine tasting experience at an Enoteca in the historic center — such as Trimani Wine Bar (Rome's oldest) or a private sommelier-led tasting of Barolo, Brunello di Montalcino, and Super Tuscans — paired with premium charcuterie and aged cheeses.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or visit Pasticceria Regoli (Esquilino) for Rome's legendary maritozzo con la panna — a sweet cream-filled bun that is a Roman institution.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Osteria dell'Enoteca or a premium Prati restaurant — try Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio for a refined midday Roman feast with wine pairings.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Pergola (Rome Cavalieri Hotel) — Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant, offering a transcendent tasting menu by Chef Heinz Beck with panoramic city views. The ultimate luxury dining experience in Rome — book months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola is the crown jewel of Roman fine dining and requires reservations far in advance — confirm before departure. Smart dress code required. The restaurant is a short taxi ride from Borgo. This is the ideal evening for a special celebration or milestone dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — revisit your favorite neighborhood at a relaxed pace. Sunday morning in Trastevere is magical with the weekly Porta Portese flea market (07:00–14:00) offering antiques, vintage art prints, and Roman curiosities. Browse for unique souvenirs — original prints of Roman ruins, vintage maps, or artisan leather goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last afternoon for any missed sights or pure leisure. Consider a private boat tour on the Tiber River for a unique perspective on Rome's ancient bridges and waterfront, or a final visit to a beloved piazza — Navona, Farnese, or the Trevi Fountain (toss your coin for a guaranteed return). Pack, check out, and arrange your private chauffeur transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell aperitivo at the hotel bar or a nearby rooftop terrace — raise a final Negroni or Bellini to an extraordinary week in the Eternal City before your departure transfer.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent hotel breakfast or a pilgrimage to Sant'Eustachio il Caffè near the Pantheon — widely considered Rome's finest espresso, a bucket-list coffee experience.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Ristorante Pierluigi (Piazza de' Ricci) — a beloved outdoor terrace restaurant near Campo de' Fiori, perfect for a long, celebratory final Roman lunch with seafood, pasta, and excellent wine.
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the airport or an early evening bite near the hotel before your transfer — a simple pizza margherita from a trusted Prati pizzeria as a final authentic Roman farewell.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and arrange the private airport transfer the night before. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for Rome's Fiumicino airport. Pack any purchased food items (truffle products, olive oil, wine) carefully in checked luggage per airline regulations. Consider purchasing a premium food hamper from Eataly Roma as a final gift or souvenir.
